title: Druva admin and API credential changes
volume: None on a normal day. Admins and API credentials change a few times a year.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Two custom detection rules for Druva, on the CloudAudit records the library's Druva parsers write from Druva Cloud Platform events. They make a detection when someone creates a Druva administrator or API credentials, the takeover that comes before backups get deleted. Each rule matches sensor type Druva Cloud Platform only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Druva parsers and the example bridge in bridges/druva-platform-events first, then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write the event type, such as Administrator Created, as the event name and the admin who made the change as the user.
- The rules take Administrator Created, API Credentials Created and API Credentials Key Regenerated from Druva's Cloud Platform events reference.

Tuning:
- If an automation creates API credentials as part of its setup, leave its admin out in the query itself, such as and user_name != 'backup-automation@example.com'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for that account as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 6 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 16 to 23 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only sample sign-ins on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.
- The events went in through bridges/druva-platform-events, run once on the lab machine against a local mock of the Druva Events API that served the sample events, and posted to HTTP Ingest as gzipped NDJSON, the way the bridge's README says.

Known gaps:
- The bridge polls, so detections arrive up to one poll interval after the event.
- An existing administrator given a higher role (Administrator Updated) isn't taken.
